decision_clues.source_quote: Reflective multilayer coatings based on two dielectrics have higher peak performance but lower out-ofband rejection than Al/MgF 2 transmittance filters. The main material combinations are (MgF 2 or AlF 3 )/(LaF 3 or GdF 3 ).
decision_clues.structure_or_method: All-dielectric reflective multilayers using fluoride pairs.
decision_clues.physical_effect: High peak reflectance/transmittance in UV; trade-off in out-of-band rejection width.
conditions_and_unknowns: Source discusses reflective mirrors or Al-based filters; task requires all-dielectric transmission filters.
LaF3/GdF3 are not in the execution inventory; MgF2 is available.
Specific layer counts for broad stopbands not detailed.
decision_clues.inference_bridge: Transfer the principle of using low-absorption fluorides (MgF2) paired with a higher-index stable oxide (Al2O3/HfO2) to construct a bandpass filter, accepting that wider stopbands may require more layers or specific stacking sequences.

decision_clues.source_quote: To achieve an arbitrary BW, the refractive indices of the coating materials must be changed... assume that the high-index material is Nb 2 O 5 with n H = 2.25... and the low-index material is SiO 2 with n L = 1.45
decision_clues.structure_or_method: Refractive index contrast manipulation for bandwidth control.
decision_clues.physical_effect: Higher index contrast enables broader stopbands or narrower passbands depending on design.
conditions_and_unknowns: Source targets 1550 nm; UV indices and dispersion will differ.
SiO2 absorption edge may be relevant below 200nm, but likely acceptable at 255nm.
Nb2O5 is in the execution inventory.
decision_clues.inference_bridge: Utilize the high index contrast between Nb2O5 (or HfO2/Ta2O5) and MgF2/SiO2 to maximize the stopband width covering 300-1100 nm with fewer layers.

routes.claim: A symmetric Fabry-Perot cavity using MgF2 spacers and Nb2O5 mirrors can isolate the 255-280 nm band, leveraging high index contrast to widen the rejection bands towards visible and NIR.
transfer_assumptions: Nb2O5 and MgF2 maintain sufficient transparency and index contrast at 255 nm despite source data being at visible/NIR wavelengths.
A single-cavity design can provide adequate rejection across the broad 300-1100 nm range without exceeding 30 layers.

expectations.controlled_conditions: Same stack symmetry, materials, and substrate.
expectations.reason: Baseline is tuned for peak; candidate adjusts mirror thicknesses primarily to affect stopband width, potentially slightly shifting but maintaining high UV transmission.

routes.model_knowledge_rationale: Standard thin-film theory suggests that increasing the number of periods in the Bragg mirrors surrounding the cavity deepens the stopband. The specific thickness values are estimated based on quarter-wave optical thickness at the center of the UV passband (~267 nm), adjusted for the available material indices.
